scope: four-node assembled chirality source and structural theorem

structural_theorem.statement: For h=(*dZ_A)⊙(*dZ_B) at λ=1, the four-node chirality-odd assembled source is Σ_j w_j ε_j s_j (π²/2). For mixed-diagonal (ε_j=s_j), this equals Σ w_j > 0. For all-same with equal scales, it equals 0.
structural_theorem.mechanism: The node-sign vector s=(+1,-1,-1,+1) COINCIDES with the mixed chirality assignment. This converts a signed alternating sum into an unsigned total.

lambda_1_TT_eigenspace.reason: Only the axial mode has V₀=0 and fully-mixed V₂ jet. Equatorial modes have V₀≠0 and zero V₂ chirality source difference.

implications: The axial mode provides a STRUCTURAL mechanism for chirality-dependent inter-node coupling that cannot be cancelled by scale choices in the mixed-diagonal construction.
The all-same construction with equal scales (consistent with the known KE degeneration for Bl₅P²) sees zero contribution from this mode.
This does not yet determine the full Ozuch coefficient: higher eigenspaces, negative modes, gauge corrections, and constant-jet receiver terms remain.
The structural theorem is exact for the V₂ boundary pairing; V₀ × V₂ cross-terms and curved corrections could modify it.
P h = h > 0, so the nonzero source is not a solvability obstruction; it produces a definite correction field whose feedback into the radial equations is the physical content.
